answer: Robots that wander cliffs use a vault for ledge scans. Proposal: each ID/day stores 1 GiB of distinct registry-encrypted blocks. A trusted registry checks unpredictable ID/day-bound reads against committed hashes under a short deadline; failure denies listing. Assume incompressible ciphertext and no audit-time refetch. Sampling can miss deletion; cheap disks weaken deterrence. Disks are reusable capital; rental and power recur; no stake. Ten compliant IDs retain 10 GiB that day: shared disks and parallel audits cannot credit a block twice.
